solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pâté formed into mound makes fridge cooler

indicators.note: the rearranged spread goes into the mound, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a hump is a small mound

indicators.note: the letters of the spread are formed into a new shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe of sorts: shaping pâté into a mound is somehow what chills the fridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formed' is the anagram signal and 'into' the container signal; 'makes' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrigerator works by a device that pumps heat out of the cabinet, which is what keeps it cold.

clue.text: Wine Society leaves jar

indicators.note: Society leaves, that is departs from, the synonym for jar

parts.note: a jar is a jolt or shock

explanation.surface: A wine society abandons its storage jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb with a jar as its object, but it removes S from SHOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is the traditional British name for German white wine from the Rhine.

clue.text: Topless brothel-keeper expelled gardener

indicators.note: without its top, the first letter of the brothel-keeper word is cut off

parts.note: a madam runs a brothel

explanation.surface: A scandal: a topless brothel-keeper threw out the gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' reads as racy description but drops the first letter from MADAM. 'expelled gardener' is the definition, not an action.
explanation.definitionFit: The first man tended the Garden of Eden and was driven out of it after the Fall.

clue.text: Miles to follow own special post at Universal Oil

indicators.note: Miles comes after the rest, so its letter goes at the end

parts.note: a pet is one's own special favourite
a post or position is a role
U is the film classification for Universal

explanation.surface: Miles is told to take over a special post at a company called Universal Oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miles' looks like a man's name but is the abbreviation M.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude mineral oil drawn from the ground is the substance refined into fuels.

clue.text: Plug hole in motorway certain to produce accident

parts.note: M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI in crosswords

indicators.note: the plug and hole pair sits in the motorway-plus-certain string

parts.note: certain means sure
a plug is an advert, shortened to AD
a vent is a hole letting air through

explanation.surface: Plugging a pothole in the motorway is sure to cause a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London-to-Leeds motorway; read as MI it starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Misadventure is mishap or bad luck, as in a coroner's verdict of death by misadventure.

clue.text: Girl in leather rejected companion?

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the whole string is read backwards
the girl's name goes in the leather word

parts.note: to leather someone is to beat them, to lam them
Una is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl in leather turns away her partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leather' is a verb meaning thrash, not the material; 'rejected' reverses the whole assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: Handbooks are often titled 'Companion', so a guidebook can be called one; the question mark flags the indirect sense.

clue.text: Tool that cuts inside metal for so long

indicators.note: the cutting tool sits inside the metal symbol

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is a tool for cutting or stamping shapes

explanation.surface: A cutting tool working inside metal for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are ways of saying goodbye; the French word is borrowed into English as a farewell.

clue.text: Turned over team coming in ahead, then losing

parts.note: a side that is up is ahead
a side is a team
to be down is to be losing

explanation.surface: A sports report: a team ahead, then losing, has been turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's sporting terms 'ahead' and 'losing' are UP and DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flipped so its top faces the floor is inverted, the phrase meaning overturned.

clue.text: Only remaining chance to take seaside town

parts.note: to last is to take, as in 'the job will take a week'
a seaside town is a holiday resort

explanation.surface: A seaside town as the one remaining chance to get away.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the final option tried when everything else has failed.

clue.text: Worker's champion bordering on clownish talent

indicators.note: the borders of the word clownish, its first and last letters, are used

parts.note: a talent is a gifted performer, an artist

explanation.surface: A workers' champion who is close to a clown in talent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chartists were a 1830s–40s British movement campaigning for working men's votes.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartism was a nineteenth-century British working-class reform movement, so its members championed workers.

clue.text: Serious drinkers call for rescue after swim

indicators.note: the rescue call comes after the swim

parts.note: a dip is a short swim
SOS is the distress signal

explanation.surface: Drinkers who went swimming and then needed rescuing.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for dipsomaniacs, it is slang for alcoholics, people who drink heavily.

clue.text: Treated unfairly as brusque Conservative put to death

parts.note: a brusque reply is a short one
hanged means executed on the gallows

explanation.surface: A curt Tory executed: hardly fair treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given too little money in return is the literal sense, extended to any unfair dealing.

clue.text: Elderly ought to visit church — right for silent treatment

indicators.note: the elderly and ought words visit, that is go into, the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
elderly means old
ought means should

explanation.surface: An old person ought to go to church, and that is the right response to being ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately ignoring someone, refusing to speak, is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Writer back on track is boss here — that's understood

indicators.note: the writer's word is put back, reading in reverse

parts.note: the setter calls themself me
a track is a path
on a newspaper, where this crossword appears, the boss is the editor, ED

explanation.surface: A writer back on track, with the boss saying that's understood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is the setter, so ME; 'boss here' points to the newspaper's editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To have shared and grasped another's feelings is a sympathetic form of understanding.

clue.text: Tips on apparel seen in one national or another.

indicators.note: the tips are seen inside the first national

parts.note: a citizen of Austria is one example of a national

indicators.note: the tips of the word apparel are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Clothing tips seen on one nationality or another.
explanation.walkthrough: The inserted letters turn one nationality into a different one, which is why 'another' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the Commonwealth country down under is a second, different nationality from the one in the wordplay.

clue.text: Married Yorkshire banker — something clicked!

parts.note: the Ouse is a Yorkshire river, and a river has banks

explanation.surface: A married Yorkshire bank manager when things suddenly fell into place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is a crossword word for a river; the Ouse flows through York.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer's pointing device is operated by being clicked.

clue.text: Play-maker, current in Peru side, taken out

indicators.note: the current symbol goes in the rearranged letters
taken out suggests the letters are knocked out of order and rearranged

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A football commentary: a playmaker in the Peru side is substituted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out' rearranges PERU SIDE, and I goes into the result.
explanation.definitionFit: He was an ancient Athenian tragedian who wrote dramas such as Medea, so a writer of plays.

clue.text: Winger's progress taking English past Ireland

indicators.note: English goes past, after, the Ireland word

parts.note: to progress is to pass on
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A rugby winger making progress, getting the English past Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' looks like a sports position but means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Passerines are perching birds, the songbird order, and a bird is a creature with wings.

clue.text: Unconscious in car

definitions.meaning: an unconscious action is done without thought, reflexively
a car with self-changing gears is called this for short

explanation.surface: Someone knocked out in their car.
explanation.definitionFit: Involuntary or reflex actions happen without conscious control; a car without a manual gearbox shares the name.

clue.text: Seamstress among those we recommend

indicators.note: the letters sit among the words that follow, spanning them

explanation.surface: A seamstress is among the people we recommend.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sews, the agent noun of the verb, is a person stitching, like a seamstress.

clue.text: One disappoints scrap-dealer on essential part

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: the heart is the core or essential part
a breaker's yard deals in scrap

explanation.surface: A scrap merchant who lets you down over a vital component.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wins affection and then lets their admirers down is called this.

clue.text: Home supporter on course for keeping record

indicators.note: the supporter keeps, holds within, the record

parts.note: on a golf course the ball is supported by a tee
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A home fan at the racecourse keeping a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home supporter' looks like one phrase, but 'Home' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a conical tent dwelling of the Plains peoples of North America, so a home.

clue.text: Here camels roaming spit on one

parts.note: gob is slang for spit
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Camels roaming here spit on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The great desert of Mongolia and China is home to wild Bactrian camels.

clue.text: Our planes and ships in spacious accommodation

parts.note: British Airways, the home airline, is BA
RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's own ships

explanation.surface: National aircraft and ships housed in a roomy space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our' in a British paper means British: BA is British Airways, RN the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm outbuilding is proverbially large, as in 'a great barn of a place'.

clue.text: Mole protects Philby revealing much

indicators.note: the mole word protects, surrounds, the Philby name

parts.note: a mole is a planted spy
Kim Philby was the British double agent

explanation.surface: A mole shields Philby, who reveals a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: Kim Philby was a British intelligence officer who spied for the Soviets.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty clothing covers little, so it reveals a lot of the body.

clue.text: Roman has drink with Greek in perfect setting

indicators.note: the perfect word forms a setting around the Greek abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: A1 means perfect, written AI
cola is a soft drink

explanation.surface: A Roman having a drink with a Greek in ideal surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnaeus Julius Agricola was a Roman general and governor of Britain.

clue.text: Foreign gentleman leading an ass

parts.note: Don is a Spanish title for a gentleman
key means leading or chief

explanation.surface: A foreign gentleman leading a donkey along.
explanation.definitionFit: Ass is the other name for the same animal, a domestic beast of burden.

clue.text: Grip had to change with racket drawn back

indicators.note: had is made to change, its letters reordered
drawn back means the racket word is pulled backwards, read in reverse

parts.note: racket means din, noise

explanation.surface: A tennis player changing grip with the racket drawn back for a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' rearranged gives ADH; NOISE reversed gives ESION.
explanation.definitionFit: The sticking of one surface to another is a kind of grip or hold.
